title: Simplify PluginSection.packages field from Option<Vec<String>> to Vec<String>
description:
Background: The packages feature (PR #123) added a `packages` field to `PluginSection` in `crates/core/src/config.rs` (line 92-93):

    #[serde(default)]
    pub packages: Option<Vec<String>>,

Problem: This is inconsistent with every other defaultable list field in the same codebase. Compare with `copy: Vec<String>` in `PluginAssets` (line 40), `vertebrae: Vec<String>` in `Spine` (line 22), and `formats`, `copy`, `font_dirs` in `RheoConfigRaw` — all use `Vec<String>` with `#[serde(default)]`, not `Option<Vec<String>>`. An empty vec and None are semantically identical here (both mean 'no packages configured'), so the Option wrapper adds no value and is noise.

Fix:
1. Change the field in `crates/core/src/config.rs` line 92-93 from:
     `pub packages: Option<Vec<String>>`
   to:
     `pub packages: Vec<String>`
2. Update the `packages()` accessor at line 283-285 from:
     `self.packages.as_deref().unwrap_or(&[])`
   to:
     `&self.packages`
   (or just `self.packages.as_slice()`)

No changes needed to callers — the `packages()` return type `&[String]` stays the same.

Expected outcome: `cargo test` passes. The field is consistent with the rest of the config codebase.
close_reason: Changed packages field to Vec<String> with #[serde(default)], updated accessor to return &self.packages

## Quality improvements over issue description

### `run_compat`: use `cargo run -p rheo-cli` not `CARGO_BIN_EXE_rheo`
The existing harness (harness.rs) universally uses `cargo run -p rheo-cli`. CARGO_BIN_EXE_rheo is not referenced anywhere in the test suite. Match the existing pattern for consistency.

### `patch_rheo_version`: line-by-line key match, no regex
Read the file, iterate lines, match `line.trim_start().splitn(2, '=').next().unwrap_or("").trim() == "version"`, replace matched lines with `format!("version = \"{version}\"")`. Rejoin with `"\n"`. No regex dependency needed.

### `patch_rheo_version`: preserve trailing newline
`str::lines()` strips the final newline. After rejoining, append `"\n"` if `content.ends_with('\n')`. Without this, rheo.toml is silently corrupted on write.

### Error messages: include file path
Use `unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("Failed to read {}: {e}", toml_path.display()))` instead of bare `.expect("...")` so failures identify which file caused the problem.

### `compat.rs`: combine rheo-0uv skeleton + rheo-3cr repos in one step
There is no value in shipping an empty `smoke_tests! {}` as a separate commit. The macro definition and the 5 repo entries are trivially small and belong together.

title: Design error handling strategy
Add structured logging with tracing
Warn when a #link call's URL argument cannot be statically resolved for transformation
description:
## Background

After rheo-8n4 and rheo-8n5 are implemented, there will still be patterns that Rheo cannot statically transform:
- Wrapper functions defined in a different file (`#import "./macros.typ": chapter-ref`)
- URL computed at runtime: `#link("./ch" + chapter_num + ".typ")`
- Variable bound conditionally or in a nested scope

Currently these cases are silently skipped — the link passes through with its `.typ` extension, producing a broken href in HTML/EPUB output. The user gets no indication that anything went wrong.

This issue adds a `tracing::warn!()` call when a `#link()` call (or any call to a known-named function "link") has a first argument that is not a string literal and could not be resolved via wrapper detection or let-binding resolution.

## Relevant files

- `crates/core/src/reticulate/parser.rs` — detection point: when `parse_link_call` returns `None` due to a non-Str arg
- `crates/core/src/reticulate/transformer.rs` — alternative: warn in `transform_source()` by running a separate scan AFTER normal extraction
- `crates/core/src/world.rs` — `transform_links()` at line ~316 is the call site; file ID / path context is available here

Preferred location: emit the warning inside `parser.rs` during the traversal pass, where we have the AST node and can compute source position. Use `eprintln!` or `tracing::warn!` — check which tracing macros are used elsewhere in the codebase (`tracing::info!`, `tracing::debug!` etc. in `compile.rs`, `world.rs`) and match that style.

## What to warn on

Warn when ALL of the following are true:
1. A `FuncCall` node has `Ident("link")` as its identifier (only direct `#link()` calls, not unknown wrapper calls — we can't know if an unknown function is link-related)
2. The first positional argument exists (the call has at least one arg) but is NOT `SyntaxKind::Str`
3. The argument is `SyntaxKind::Ident` AND the ident is not in the `UrlBindingMap` (i.e. it wasn't resolved by rheo-8n5)
4. The argument is any other non-Str expression (FuncCall, BinaryOp, etc.)

Do NOT warn when:
- The `#link` call's first arg is a non-string that resolves correctly (handled by rheo-8n4/rheo-8n5)
- The `#link` call appears inside a `Raw` code block (already skipped by the serializer)
- The first arg is a label reference `<label>` (valid non-string link target)

## Warning message format

```
tracing::warn!(
    file = %current_file.display(),
    "rheo: #link() call has a non-literal URL argument that cannot be statically transformed. \
     The .typ extension will NOT be rewritten in the output. \
     To fix: use a string literal directly: #link(\"./file.typ\")[...], \
     or define the wrapper function in the same file."
);
```

Include the approximate source position if feasible (line number from the node's span via `source.range(span).start` — this gives a byte offset; convert to line number via `source.byte_to_line(offset)`).

## Steps

1. In the traversal inside `extract_links_from_node` (or in a new dedicated `scan_for_unresolvable_links()` function), after failing to extract a `LinkInfo` from a `FuncCall` with `Ident("link")`:
   - Check if the failure was due to a non-Str first arg (distinguish from "not a link call at all")
   - If yes and the conditions above are met, emit `tracing::warn!`

2. The warning must carry the `current_file` path. `extract_links()` currently only takes `&Source`. Add a `current_file: Option<&Path>` parameter (default `None` for detached/test usage) OR pass it through `transform_source()` which already has `current_file: &Path`.

   Simplest approach: add a `warn_unresolvable: bool` flag and `current_file: &Path` parameter to `transform_source()` only — warnings are only useful during real compilation, not in unit tests. The warning scan can be a separate pass after `extract_links()` returns, keeping the existing signature unchanged.

3. Add a test that `transform_source()` does NOT panic or error on unresolvable links (just silently skips with a warning), confirming the graceful degradation:
```rust
#[test]
fn test_unresolvable_link_does_not_error() {
    let source = r#"#link(compute_url())[text]"#;
    let transformer = LinkTransformer::new("html");
    // Should succeed; unresolvable link passes through unchanged
    let result = transformer.transform_source(source, Path::new("test.typ"), Path::new("/root"));
    assert!(result.is_ok());
    assert!(result.unwrap().contains("#link(compute_url())"));
}
```

## Expected outcome

When a user has `#link(url)` where `url` is an unresolvable expression, Rheo prints a `WARN` log line during compilation naming the file and explaining the issue. No error is raised; the link passes through unchanged. The user can then diagnose and fix their source.
acceptance_criteria:
- `RUST_LOG=rheo=warn cargo run -- compile ...` shows a warning for unresolvable `#link` URL args
- Warning names the source file
- Compilation still succeeds (warning only, no error)
- Unresolvable links pass through to output unchanged
- No warnings for resolved links (literal strings, wrapper-detected, let-bound)
- No warnings for `#link` calls inside raw code blocks
- `cargo test` passes, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` is clean
close_reason: Added tracing::warn! for unresolvable #link() URL args (non-literal, non-label, unbound ident). Warning carries file and line, compilation succeeds, unresolvable links pass through unchanged. Tests added.

title: Register 5 GitHub repos as compatibility tests
description:
## Background

This issue depends on rheo-0uv (compatibility test infrastructure). Once that infrastructure is in place, this issue registers the 5 known real-world Rheo project repos as smoke test cases.

## Goal

Populate the `smoke_tests!` invocation in `crates/tests/tests/compat.rs` with the 5 known real-world Rheo project repos. Each entry is `(name, url)` — the macro auto-generates `smoke_<name>` as the test function name and uses `stringify!(name)` as the clone directory. Adding or removing a repo is a single-line edit.

## Implementation

In `crates/tests/tests/compat.rs`, replace `smoke_tests! {}` with:

```rust
smoke_tests! {
    (maths_ohrg_org,            "https://github.com/freecomputinglab/maths.ohrg.org"),
    (rheo_ohrg_org,             "https://github.com/freecomputinglab/rheo.ohrg.org"),
    (freecomputinglab_ohrg_org, "https://github.com/freecomputinglab/freecomputinglab.ohrg.org"),
    (lolm_ohrg_org,             "https://github.com/freecomputinglab/lolm.ohrg.org"),
    (digitaltheory_dot_org,     "https://github.com/digitaltheorylab/digitaltheory-dot-org"),
}
```

Each `name` is the repo slug (last URL path segment with `.` replaced by `_`). The macro (defined in rheo-0uv) expands this into individual `#[test]` functions named `smoke_maths_ohrg_org`, `smoke_rheo_ohrg_org`, etc.

**To add a repo:** append one `(name, url)` line.  
**To remove a repo:** delete its line.

## Acceptance criteria

- `cargo test --test compat` (no env var) still passes immediately with 0 tests run (all return early)
- `RUN_COMPAT_TESTS=1 cargo test --test compat` clones all 5 repos, compiles them, and all tests pass
- Any compilation error in any repo causes that test function to panic with the full rheo compile output
- Adding/removing a repo requires editing exactly one line in `smoke_tests! { ... }`

Add CI job for scheduled compat tests
description:
## Background

This issue depends on rheo-3cr (registered compat tests). The compat tests require network access and take non-trivial time (cloning 5 repos + compiling). They must NOT run on every PR — only on a schedule or on-demand.

## Goal

Add a separate GitHub Actions job to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that runs the compat test suite on a schedule (nightly) and can also be triggered manually via `workflow_dispatch`.

## Implementation

In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, add a new top-level job (do NOT modify the existing main CI job). The new job should:

1. Trigger on:
   - `schedule`: nightly (e.g. `cron: '0 2 * * *'` — 2am UTC, off-peak)
   - `workflow_dispatch`: allows manual triggering from the GitHub Actions UI

2. Job definition (name it `compat`):
   ```yaml
   compat:
     name: Compatibility tests
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
       - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
       - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
       - name: Run compatibility tests
         run: cargo test --test compat
         env:
           RUN_COMPAT_TESTS: "1"
           TYPST_IGNORE_SYSTEM_FONTS: "1"
   ```

3. The existing `test` job in ci.yml must NOT be modified — it should continue running on every push/PR without `RUN_COMPAT_TESTS`.

## Reference

Look at the existing `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for the rust-toolchain and rust-cache step versions already in use — use the same versions for consistency. Do not introduce new action versions that aren't already in the file unless necessary.

## Acceptance criteria

- The existing CI job is unchanged
- A new `compat` job appears in the Actions tab when triggered manually or on the nightly schedule
- The nightly schedule does not interfere with PR-based CI runs
- `cargo test --test compat` is NOT run in the existing main test job
design:
## Quality improvement: create `.github/workflows/compat.yml` instead of modifying `ci.yml`

The issue says to add a `schedule:` trigger and a `compat` job inside `ci.yml`. This has an unintended side-effect: adding `schedule:` to `ci.yml` causes the entire workflow — including the expensive `ci` job (fmt + clippy + full test suite) — to run nightly, wasting CI minutes.

**Better approach:** create a new, dedicated `.github/workflows/compat.yml` file with only `schedule:` and `workflow_dispatch:` as triggers, containing only the `compat` job. The existing `ci.yml` is left completely untouched.

The action versions (`actions/checkout@v4`, `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable`, `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2`) must match those already in `ci.yml` exactly.

title: Implement output directory management
Resolve let-bound URL variables used as #link arguments
description:
## Background

When a `.typ` URL is stored in a `let` binding and then passed to `#link`, the current parser silently skips it:

```typst
#let url = "./ch02.typ"
#link(url)[Chapter 2]   // first arg is SyntaxKind::Ident, not SyntaxKind::Str → skipped
```

`extract_first_string_arg()` in `parser.rs:65-74` iterates the `Args` node looking for `SyntaxKind::Str` children only. When it finds `SyntaxKind::Ident("url")` instead, it returns `None` and the link is never registered for transformation. The output HTML/EPUB will contain a broken `.typ` href.

This issue extends the pre-pass framework introduced in rheo-8n4 to also collect constant let-bound string values, and follows the variable reference at the `#link()` call site.

## Relevant files

- `crates/core/src/reticulate/parser.rs` — add `collect_url_bindings()` to the pre-pass; update `extract_first_string_arg()` fallback path
- `crates/core/src/reticulate/types.rs` — `LinkInfo` (already has `is_wrapper_call` from rheo-8n4; no new fields needed)
- `crates/core/src/reticulate/transformer.rs` — no changes needed if `LinkInfo.byte_range` points to the correct location

## Strategy: rewrite at the let-binding site, not at the call site

When `#link(url)` is encountered, we cannot replace `url` with a literal in the call — that would change a variable reference to a string, breaking the variable's other uses. Instead, the transformation target is the **string literal inside the let binding**:

```
#let url = "./ch02.typ"   ←  byte_range points HERE (the Str node)
#link(url)[Chapter 2]
```

After transformation:
```
#let url = "./ch02.html"  ←  rewritten
#link(url)[Chapter 2]     ←  unchanged, but now resolves to .html
```

This is valid because `ReplaceStringLiteralInPlace` (introduced in rheo-8n4) replaces only the Str node bytes at any given byte_range.

**Limitation**: if the same variable is used both as a link URL and in non-link content (e.g. displayed as text), rewriting the let binding changes both uses. This is a known edge case; document it in a code comment.

## Steps

### Step 1 — Add `collect_url_bindings()` to `parser.rs`

```rust
/// Maps let-binding name → (url_string, byte_range_of_str_node_in_source)
/// Only captures simple constant bindings: `#let x = "./something.typ"` at file scope.
pub type UrlBindingMap = HashMap<String, (String, Range<usize>)>;

pub fn collect_url_bindings(root: &SyntaxNode) -> UrlBindingMap {
    let mut map = HashMap::new();
    collect_bindings_from_node(root, root, &mut map, 0);
    map
}
```

`collect_bindings_from_node` traverses the AST. For each `LetBinding` node:
1. Find the `Ident` child — that is the binding name
2. Find the next non-whitespace sibling or child — if it is `SyntaxKind::Str`, this is a constant string binding
3. Check `is_relative_typ_link(unquoted_value)` from `validator.rs` — only record if it looks like a `.typ` path (avoids polluting the map with every string binding)
4. Calculate the byte offset of the `Str` node using `calculate_node_offset()` (already in `parser.rs:119-143`)
5. Record `map.insert(name, (unquoted_value, str_node_byte_range))`

Skip `LetBinding` nodes that are inside a `Closure` body or a `CodeBlock` — only top-level (file-scope) bindings are supported in this issue. Detecting scope depth: track whether the traversal has passed through a `Closure` or `CodeBlock` node.

### Step 2 — Update `extract_links()` to pass `UrlBindingMap` into the traversal

`extract_links()` already runs `collect_link_wrappers()` before the traversal (from rheo-8n4). Add:
```rust
let url_bindings = collect_url_bindings(&root);
extract_links_from_node(&root, &root, &mut links, &wrappers, &url_bindings);
```

### Step 3 — Update `parse_link_call` for the `#link(ident)` case

After resolving `url_param_index` and calling `extract_nth_string_arg(args, url_param_index)`:
- If it returns `Some(...)` (literal string), proceed as before
- If it returns `None`, check whether the arg at `url_param_index` is `SyntaxKind::Ident`
  - If yes, look up the ident text in `url_bindings`
  - If found: create `LinkInfo` with `url = binding.url_string`, `byte_range = binding.str_byte_range`, `is_wrapper_call = true` (reuse the flag — semantically: "use ReplaceStringLiteralInPlace, not full call reconstruction")
  - If not found: return `None` (unresolvable; will be caught by the warning issue)

### Step 4 — Add tests in `parser.rs`

```rust
#[test]
fn test_let_bound_url_resolved() {
    let source = Source::detached(r#"
        #let dest = "./ch02.typ"
        #link(dest)[Chapter 2]
    "#);
    let links = extract_links(&source);
    assert_eq!(links.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(links[0].url, "./ch02.typ");
}

#[test]
fn test_let_bound_url_not_typ_ignored() {
    // Only .typ bindings are tracked
    let source = Source::detached(r#"
        #let url = "https://example.com"
        #link(url)[external]
    "#);
    let links = extract_links(&source);
    // External URL: url binding not in map, link still extracted via normal path
    // (url is not a .typ link so even if extracted it would be KeepOriginal)
    assert_eq!(links.len(), 0);  // not extracted at all — ident arg, no binding match
}

#[test]
fn test_let_bound_url_rewritten_in_binding() {
    // Integration: transform_source rewrites the let binding string, not the call site
    let source = r#"
        #let dest = "./ch02.typ"
        #link(dest)[Chapter 2]
    "#;
    use crate::reticulate::transformer::LinkTransformer;
    let transformer = LinkTransformer::new("html");
    let result = transformer.transform_source(source, Path::new("ch01.typ"), Path::new("/root")).unwrap();
    assert!(result.contains("\"./ch02.html\""));
    assert!(result.contains("#link(dest)"));  // call site unchanged
}
```

## Expected outcome

`#link(dest)` where `dest` is a file-scope let binding containing a `.typ` path produces a correctly rewritten binding value after `transform_source()`. The call site `#link(dest)` is left untouched.

## Known limitations

- Only file-scope `let` bindings are tracked. Bindings inside functions, blocks, or conditionals are ignored.
- If the same variable is used both as a link URL and rendered as text, the text will also show the rewritten extension. Rare in practice; document in a code comment.
- Variables defined in imported files are not followed.
acceptance_criteria:
- `#link(var)` where `var` is a file-scope `let` binding to a `.typ` path is rewritten correctly
- The let binding value is rewritten; the `#link(var)` call site is unchanged
- Non-`.typ` bindings and out-of-scope bindings are not tracked
- All existing tests still pass
- New tests pass
- `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` is clean

title: Eliminate redundant re-parse in find_code_block_ranges
description:
## Background

During link/import transformation, `LinkTransformer::transform_source()` (`crates/core/src/reticulate/transformer.rs:40-87`) calls two reticulate functions in sequence:

1. `parser::extract_nodes(&source_obj)` — uses the `Source` object's pre-parsed AST (no redundant parse)
2. `serializer::find_code_block_ranges(&source_obj)` — accepts `&Source` but internally calls `typst::syntax::parse(source.text())` (line 80 of `crates/core/src/reticulate/serializer.rs`), discarding the existing AST and re-parsing the full source text

This means every source file processed by rheo triggers two Typst parses inside `transform_source` (one in `Source::detached()` at transformer.rs:48, one in `find_code_block_ranges`), plus a third parse when Typst itself compiles the transformed source. The second parse is entirely avoidable.

## Files

- **`crates/core/src/reticulate/serializer.rs`** — contains `find_code_block_ranges` (lines 79-84) and `collect_raw_ranges` (lines 86-102)

## Steps

1. Open `crates/core/src/reticulate/serializer.rs`.
2. Change `find_code_block_ranges` (lines 79-84) from:
   ```rust
   pub fn find_code_block_ranges(source: &Source) -> Vec<Range<usize>> {
       let root = typst::syntax::parse(source.text());
       let mut ranges = Vec::new();
       collect_raw_ranges(&root, &mut ranges, 0);
       ranges
   }
   ```

   pub fn find_code_block_ranges(source: &Source) -> Vec<Range<usize>> {

       ranges
   }

4. Run `cargo test` — all tests must pass.

One fewer Typst parse per source file per compilation across all modes (per-file, merged PDF, HTML, EPUB). No behaviour change — `source.root()` returns the same parsed tree that `typst::syntax::parse(source.text())` would produce.

## Background

In `crates/core/src/reticulate/spine.rs`, for each spine file rheo currently performs at least two separate AST parses:
1. `extract_label_and_title()` — parses source to find the document title
2. `transform_source()` — calls `extract_links()` (and after rheo-8m2, `extract_imports()`) which each parse the source again

For large books with many spine files this is unnecessary repeated work. The fix is to merge `extract_links()` and `extract_imports()` into a single traversal, and investigate sharing the parse with `extract_label_and_title()`.

## Relevant files

- `crates/core/src/reticulate/parser.rs` — `extract_links()`, `extract_imports()`, `extract_label_and_title()` (or wherever it lives)
- `crates/core/src/reticulate/transformer.rs` — `transform_source()` calls the parser functions
- `crates/core/src/reticulate/spine.rs` — orchestrates the per-file pipeline

## Steps

1. Add a combined `extract_nodes(source: &Source) -> (Vec<LinkInfo>, Vec<ImportInfo>)` function to `parser.rs` that traverses the AST once and collects both. Update `transform_source()` to call `extract_nodes()` instead of calling `extract_links()` and `extract_imports()` separately.

2. Investigate whether `extract_label_and_title()` can accept an already-parsed `SyntaxNode` (or `Source`) to avoid re-parsing. If `extract_label_and_title()` is in a different module, expose a variant that takes a `&Source` so `spine.rs` can parse once and pass the result to both it and `transform_source()`.

3. Benchmark is not required — the improvement is structural (parse O(n) once instead of 3x). A code comment noting the intentional single-parse design is sufficient documentation.

title: Add import/include path extraction to Typst AST parser
description:
## Background

When `merge = true` in `[pdf.spine]`, rheo concatenates multiple `.typ` files into a single temporary file placed at the project root. The existing reticulate pipeline already rewrites `#link()` calls (see `crates/core/src/reticulate/parser.rs` → `extract_links()`), but `#import` and `#include` statements are not yet handled. This issue adds the AST extraction foundation; the actual rewriting is done in the next issue.

## Relevant files

- `crates/core/src/reticulate/parser.rs` — add new types and extraction function here
- `crates/core/src/reticulate/mod.rs` — may need to re-export new types
- `crates/core/src/reticulate/types.rs` — check if `LinkInfo` lives here; `ImportInfo` should follow the same pattern

## Steps

1. Define an `ImportInfo` struct in the same location as `LinkInfo`:
   ```rust
   pub struct ImportInfo {
       pub path: String,          // The raw path string (e.g. "./utils.typ" or "@preview/foo:0.1.0")
       pub byte_range: Range<usize>, // Byte range of the path string ONLY (not the whole statement)
       pub is_package: bool,      // true if path starts with '@'
   }
   ```

2. Add `extract_imports(source: &Source) -> Vec<ImportInfo>` to `parser.rs`. Model it on `extract_links()`:
   - Parse with `typst::syntax::parse(source.text())`
   - Walk the AST recursively
   - Match on `SyntaxKind::ModuleImport` and `SyntaxKind::ModuleInclude` nodes
   - For each matched node, find the first child with `SyntaxKind::Str` — that is the path argument
   - Extract the inner string value (strip surrounding quotes) and compute its byte offset within the full source using the same cumulative-offset approach as `calculate_node_offset()` in `parser.rs`
   - Set `is_package = path.starts_with('@')`

3. Add unit tests covering:
   - `#import "./utils.typ": *` (relative, non-package)
   - `#import "@preview/tablex:0.0.6": tablex` (package import — is_package = true)
   - `#include "./figures/fig1.typ"` (include)
   - An import inside a raw code block (should still be extracted — filtering happens in the serializer layer)
   - Multiple imports in one file

## Expected outcome

`extract_imports()` returns a `Vec<ImportInfo>` with correct path strings and byte ranges that can be used for in-place string replacement by the serializer.
acceptance_criteria:
- `extract_imports()` is callable and returns correct `ImportInfo` for all import/include variants
- Package imports are flagged with `is_package = true`
- Unit tests pass (`cargo test`)
- `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` is clean

title: Integration test for auto-detected manifest package assets
Fix asset collision error message to show source paths not output paths
description:
Background: The `packages` sugar feature (feat/rheopackages branch, PR #123) added `resolve_assets` in `crates/cli/src/lib.rs`. This function detects when two asset entries would produce the same output-relative path and errors with a collision message.

Problem: The collision detection at `crates/cli/src/lib.rs:511-518` stores the destination (output) path in `seen_relative_paths`, not the source path:

    seen_relative_paths.insert(rel.clone(), abs.clone());  // abs = output path

So the error message reads:
    "asset path collision: 'style.css' produced by both '/build/html/style.css' and '/build/html/style.css'"

Both paths are identical (same output destination), which is useless to the user. The message should name the *source* paths that both map to the same output.

Fix: Change `seen_relative_paths: HashMap<String, PathBuf>` to store the absolute *source* path instead of the output path. At the point of insertion, the source is available in the `sources` vec being iterated. Update the error message to say something like:
    "asset path collision: output '{rel}' would be written by both '{source_a}' and '{source_b}'"

Files to modify: `crates/cli/src/lib.rs` around lines 424 and 503-526 (the `resolve_assets` function, specifically the `outputs.into_iter().map(|abs| { ... }))` closure and the HashMap declaration above it).

Expected outcome: When two user or package asset blocks would produce the same output path, the error message clearly identifies which two source files are in conflict.

title: Rewrite relative imports during spine merge
description:
## Background

When `merge = true` in `[pdf.spine]`, rheo writes a concatenated `.typ` file to a `NamedTempFile` at the project root (`crates/core/src/plugins/mod.rs`, `NamedTempFile::new_in(&self.options.root)`). Any relative `#import` or `#include` path that was valid relative to the original file's subdirectory is now broken.

Example: `chapters/ch01.typ` contains `#import "./macros.typ": *`. After merging into a file at the project root, Typst resolves this as `<root>/macros.typ`, not `<root>/chapters/macros.typ`. Compilation fails.

This issue wires up the `extract_imports()` function from rheo-8m1 into the existing transformation pipeline so that relative paths are rewritten before concatenation.

## Relevant files

- `crates/core/src/reticulate/transformer.rs` — `transform_source()` is the entry point; `_project_root: &Path` is already a parameter but currently unused
- `crates/core/src/reticulate/serializer.rs` — `apply_transformations()` handles byte-range replacements; reuse this
- `crates/core/src/reticulate/types.rs` — `LinkTransform::ReplaceUrl { new_url }` already exists and can be reused for path rewriting
- `crates/core/src/reticulate/parser.rs` — `extract_imports()` added by rheo-8m1

## Steps

1. In `transform_source()` (`transformer.rs`), after computing link transformations, call `extract_imports()` on the already-parsed `source_obj`.

2. For each `ImportInfo` with `is_package = false`:
   - If `path` is absolute (starts with `/`), skip it
   - Otherwise compute the rewritten path:
     ```rust
     let file_dir = current_file.parent().unwrap_or(Path::new(""));
     let absolute = file_dir.join(&import.path);
     let new_path = absolute
         .strip_prefix(project_root)
         .map(|p| p.to_str().unwrap().to_owned())
         .unwrap_or(import.path.clone());
     ```
   - Produce a `LinkTransform::ReplaceUrl { new_url: new_path }` for `import.byte_range`

3. Rename `_project_root` → `project_root` to activate the parameter.

4. Collect link and import transformations into a single vec and pass them all to `serializer::apply_transformations()` in one call (the serializer already sorts by offset).

5. Ensure imports inside `Raw` code blocks are protected by the existing `find_code_block_ranges()` mechanism (verify it covers `ModuleImport`/`ModuleInclude` nodes inside raw blocks).

6. In `spine.rs`, verify that `transform_source()` is called with a non-None `project_root` when in merge mode.

## Expected outcome

A project with spine files that use relative `#import`/`#include` paths compiles successfully with `merge = true`. The rewritten paths in the merged temp file correctly point to locations relative to the project root.
acceptance_criteria:
- `cargo run -- compile <project-with-relative-imports> --pdf` succeeds when `merge = true`
- Package imports (`@preview/...`) are not modified
- Absolute paths are not modified
- Imports inside raw blocks are not modified
- `cargo test` passes, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` is clean

title: Wire auto-detected manifest packages into perform_compilation()
description:
## Background

This is part of a feature to auto-detect Rheo packages from Typst import statements. The previous issues (rheo-6j3, rheo-9dl, rheo-1hf) implemented the scanning, resolution, and manifest-reading utilities. This issue wires them into the actual compilation pipeline in crates/cli/src/lib.rs.

The entry point is perform_compilation() starting at line 623. Currently it:
1. Lines 663-667: Calls resolve_packages() for user-declared packages (from rheo.toml [html].packages)
2. Line 668: Calls plugin.map_packages_to_assets() to produce package_blocks: Vec<PackageAssets>
3. Lines 670-676: Passes package_blocks to resolve_assets()
4. Lines 686-693: Iterates package_blocks for copy_glob_patterns()

This issue extends step 2: after building package_blocks from user-declared packages, auto-detect additional PackageAssets from .typ file imports that have typst.toml manifests, and append them to package_blocks.

## Relevant existing code

- `crates/cli/src/lib.rs:623` — perform_compilation() function definition
- `crates/cli/src/lib.rs:663-702` — the section to modify (package resolution and asset resolution)
- `crates/core/src/plugins/manifest` — scan_project_package_imports(), detect_manifest_package_assets() from companion issues
- `crates/core/src/plugins::PackageAssets` — type used by both resolve_assets() and copy_glob_patterns()
- `crates/core/src/plugins::FormatPlugin::name()` — returns the format name string ("html", "pdf", "epub")
- `crates/core/src/config::PluginSection::packages()` — at crates/core/src/config.rs:282-285, returns user-declared package strings

## Steps to implement

1. In `crates/cli/src/lib.rs`, after line 668 (after `let package_blocks = plugin.map_packages_to_assets(&resolved_packages);`), insert:

```rust
// Auto-detect packages from .typ imports that have [tool.rheo.{format}] manifests
let auto_import_paths =
    rheo_core::plugins::manifest::scan_project_package_imports(&project.typ_files);
let auto_blocks = rheo_core::plugins::manifest::detect_manifest_package_assets(
    &auto_import_paths,
    plugin.name(),
    plugin_section.packages(),
);
let package_blocks: Vec<rheo_core::plugins::PackageAssets> =
    package_blocks.into_iter().chain(auto_blocks).collect();
```

2. Verify that the `copy_glob_patterns` loop at lines 686-693 still compiles correctly — it iterates `&package_blocks` and uses `package.assets.copy` and `package.source_root`. Since auto-detected blocks have `copy: vec![]`, the loop will simply do nothing for them (correct behavior).

3. Verify that `resolve_assets()` at line 670 still takes `&package_blocks` — the type is unchanged.

4. Run `cargo build` to confirm no compile errors.

5. Run `cargo test` to confirm existing tests still pass.

## Expected outcome

When a project .typ file contains `#import "@rheo/slides:0.1.0"` and that package has a typst.toml with [tool.rheo.html] declaring CSS/JS assets, running `cargo run -- compile <project> --html` produces:
- `build/html/rheo/slides/style.css` (or whichever files are declared)
- Those files referenced in the HTML output's `<head>`

title: Fix PDF merged compilation to handle per-document bibliographies
description:
## Background

`compile_pdf_merged_bundle()` (`crates/pdf/src/lib.rs:46`) intentionally wraps all spine files in a single `#document("title.pdf")[#include "a.typ" #include "b.typ" ...]` bundle entry to produce one combined PDF. This fails with "multiple bibliographies are not yet supported" when multiple spine files each declare their own `#bibliography()`.

Unlike the per-file cases (rheo-o6h, rheo-j6j), merged mode cannot be fixed by simply compiling each file independently — the output must be a single combined PDF document.

## Options to evaluate

### Option A: Compile each vertebra independently then concatenate PDFs

Compile each spine file to a `PagedDocument` using `world.compile_pdf()` (available on `RheoWorld` at `crates/core/src/world.rs:269`). Concatenate the resulting documents into a single PDF.

Check whether `typst-pdf` provides a multi-document merge/concatenate API:
- Inspect the `typst-pdf` crate's public API for any concat/merge function.
- If it exists, use it to produce the merged PDF from individually compiled `PagedDocument`s.

### Option B: Require a single bundle-entry file for merged mode

If PDF concatenation is not available from `typst-pdf`, document the limitation and return a clear user-facing error when `merge=true` and the spine contains more than one non-bundle-entry document with a bibliography. The message should explain the workaround: create a single bundle-entry `.typ` that `#include`s all files and declares one shared `#bibliography()`.

## Implementation

1. Check the `typst-pdf` crate API. Look for any function that takes multiple `PagedDocument` values or accepts a list of pages from multiple sources.
2. If Option A is viable:
   - For each `doc` in `spine.documents`, create a `RheoWorld::new(compilation_root, &doc.path, plugin_library)`, inject a per-file bundle entry (single-document TracedSpine), call `world.compile_pdf()` to get a `PagedDocument`.
   - Use the concatenation API to merge all `PagedDocument`s.
   - Serialise to bytes with `document_to_pdf_bytes()` (check `crates/core/src/compile.rs` for existing helpers) and write to `output_path`.
3. If Option B:
   - Before calling `export_bundle()`, inspect whether any spine document declares a bibliography (this may require scanning source text or simply catching the Typst error and re-surfacing a better message).
   - Or: replace the current opaque "bundle compilation had errors: multiple bibliographies..." error with an explicit check and a message like: "Merged PDF does not support multiple bibliographies. Create a single entry file that #includes all chapters and declares one shared #bibliography()."

## Acceptance criteria

Option A: `cargo run -- compile examples/blog_site --pdf` with `merge = true` in rheo.toml produces one combined PDF with all bibliographies rendered.

Option B: The same command fails with a clear, actionable error message explaining the limitation and how to resolve it (not the raw Typst error).

Either way: `cargo test` and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` pass.
close_reason: Done -- Merged PDF mode now works with context-wrapped bibliographies. Removed obsolete test_pdf_merge_duplicate_filenames test.

title: Fix PDF per-file plugin to compile each spine vertebra as a standalone document
description:
## Background

Same root cause as rheo-o6h (HTML plugin fix). The PDF per-file plugin (`compile_pdf_per_file_bundle()` in `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs:72`) calls `world.export_bundle()` on the same combined world that wraps all spine documents in one `typst::compile::<Bundle>()` pass. When multiple spine files each declare `#bibliography()`, Typst raises "multiple bibliographies are not yet supported" and compilation fails.

The fix is the same pattern as for HTML: iterate over `spine.documents` and compile each file with its own `RheoWorld`, rather than using the pre-built combined world.

## Implementation

1. **Pass the full context into `compile_pdf_bundle_impl()`.** Currently `PdfPlugin::compile()` (`crates/pdf/src/lib.rs:25`) passes only `ctx.options.world`, `ctx.options.output`, and `ctx.spine.merge` to `compile_pdf_bundle_impl()`. Extend the signature to also pass `ctx.spine` (a `&TracedSpine`) and `ctx.options.root` (the compilation root `&Path`).

2. **Refactor `compile_pdf_per_file_bundle()` to iterate per document** instead of calling `world.export_bundle()` once. For each `doc` in `spine.documents`:
   a. Create a fresh `RheoWorld::new(compilation_root, &doc.path, plugin_library)`. The `PdfPlugin.typst_library()` returns a small lemma helper — retrieve it via `PdfPlugin.typst_library()` and pass it through.
   b. Generate a per-file bundle entry via `generate_bundle_entry()` (`crates/core/src/reticulate/spine.rs:19`) for just this single document (single-document `TracedSpine`, `merge=false`). Inject it with `world.inject_bundle_entry()`.
   c. Call `world.export_bundle()` on the per-file world.
   d. Filter to `.pdf` files and write to `output_dir` — same logic as current code at `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs:84-101`.

3. **Handle `is_bundle_entry=true` documents** the same way as described in rheo-o6h: generate a bundle entry using a single-doc `TracedSpine` with `is_bundle_entry=true` — the `generate_bundle_entry()` function already emits a bare `#include` for these, which lets the file control its own bundle structure.

4. The combined `world` argument passed in from `compile_with_bundle()` (orchestrate.rs) is **not used** in the refactored per-file path. Ignore it.

## Acceptance criteria

- `cargo run -- compile examples/blog_site --pdf` (non-merged) succeeds with no errors.
- One `.pdf` file is produced per spine vertebra.
- Bibliographies in each file render correctly.
- `cargo test` passes.
- `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` passes.
close_reason: Fixed PDF per-file plugin to compile each spine vertebra independently with its own RheoWorld, resolving multiple bibliographies issue for non-merged mode.

title: Fix HTML plugin to compile each spine vertebra as a standalone document
description:
## Background

When compiling a project where multiple spine vertebrae each declare `#bibliography()`, the HTML plugin fails with Typst's error: "multiple bibliographies are not yet supported". This is a regression caused by how the HTML plugin uses the bundle API.

The HTML plugin's `compile_html_bundle()` (`crates/html/src/lib.rs:117`) calls `options.world.export_bundle()`. That world was assembled by `compile_with_bundle()` in `crates/cli/src/orchestrate.rs:52-103`. It injects a synthetic bundle entry generated by `generate_bundle_entry()` (`crates/core/src/reticulate/spine.rs:19`) that wraps every spine document in the project in a single `typst::compile::<Bundle>()` call:

```
#document("severance-ep-1.html")[#include "severance-ep-1.typ"]
#document("severance-ep-2.html")[#include "severance-ep-2.typ"]
...
```

Because all files are pulled into one compilation pass, Typst sees multiple `#bibliography()` declarations and errors. The correct behaviour is that each spine vertebra is an independent entrypoint compiled with its own `RheoWorld` — exactly as the EPUB plugin already does in `compile_epub_impl()` (`crates/epub/src/lib.rs:322-356`), where it iterates `spine.documents` and compiles each file independently.

## Implementation

1. **Pass spine info into the compile function.** Modify `HtmlPlugin::compile()` (`crates/html/src/lib.rs:102`) to pass `ctx.spine` and `ctx.options.root` (compilation root) into `compile_html_bundle()`. Currently only `ctx.options` and `ctx.config` are passed; the spine is needed to iterate documents.

2. **Refactor `compile_html_bundle()` to iterate per document** instead of calling `options.world.export_bundle()` once for everything. The new loop body for each `doc` in `spine.documents`:
   a. Build a single-document `TracedSpine` (`merge=false`, single entry with `doc`) — or just pass the document path directly.
   b. Create a fresh `RheoWorld::new(compilation_root, &doc.path, plugin_library)`. The `plugin_library` is `HtmlPlugin.typst_library()` (which returns `None` for HTML — check `crates/html/src/lib.rs`).
   c. Generate a per-file bundle entry via `generate_bundle_entry()` (`crates/core/src/reticulate/spine.rs:19`) for just this one document, then inject it with `world.inject_bundle_entry()`.
   d. Call `world.export_bundle()` to produce HTML output for this one file.
   e. Apply the existing CSS/font injection logic to each `.html` file in the output (code currently at `crates/html/src/lib.rs:141-171` — reuse it unchanged).
   f. Write output files to `options.output` directory (unchanged).

3. **Handle `is_bundle_entry=true` documents** (the `SpineDocument.is_bundle_entry` flag). For these, create a `RheoWorld` pointing directly to the file without adding a `#document()` wrapper — the file controls its own bundle structure. Generate the bundle entry with a `TracedSpine` that includes only this one `is_bundle_entry=true` document (spine.rs already handles this case by emitting a bare `#include`).

4. The combined `options.world` (the old all-files world created by `compile_with_bundle()` in orchestrate.rs) is **not used** in the refactored path. Ignore it.

## Acceptance criteria

- `cargo run -- compile examples/blog_site --html` succeeds with no errors.
- One `.html` file is produced in the output directory per spine vertebra.
- Each file's bibliography renders correctly (citations resolve within the individual document).
- `cargo test` passes.
- `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` passes.
close_reason: Fixed HTML plugin to compile each spine vertebra independently with its own RheoWorld, resolving multiple bibliographies issue.
